My Game Rating: 8.5 / 10

-Nice game-play
-Needs to use most of your brain to think of your strategy to hack.
-You need to focus well on playing this game.
-Realistic Computer Commands.

More of a imitation experience than a puzzle game, the act of hacking rarely involves skills, it's just memorization of a few commands, and only a few times it requires clever time management when being traced. I was hoping that hacking would have more of a puzzle element to get you thinking, and have big brain hacker moments instead of just typing a command and waiting for it to finish executing.

As a hacking experience it is enjoyable, as you will get immersed in the (fake) hacking communities of Hacknet, and climbing up the ranks. But since as a game it feels too lacking I honestly can't recommend it for someone who's looking for a challenging game more than a sim. I'm more middle of the road here, but Steam's review system is a binary yes or no. I guess I still enjoyed the whole game despite it's flaws and it's up to you individually to decide if the game is for you.

Don't take this review as a "Do not buy this game", it truly sucks that Steam does not have a "Mixed" score option, so since my opinion leans more toward "not recommended", I'll go for that one.

So, this is a puzzle "hacking" game. The game teaches the basics of CMD commands and gives you a couple of tools to deal with different protections. You hack a computer, scan for more computers or clues and keep going until you get what you want. Some jobs require going through multiple computers, copying files, uploading stuff.

The problem is that there is little challenge to it. All the hack programs do things automatically, so you just have to wait until they finish doing their work while you watch a big red timer counting down and hope everything goes fast enough. It certainly gives that rush of "almost got caught" feeling, but it does get stale after some point.

The little bit of story is pretty good, it does give you the sensation of "saving the world", but all you did was wait for timers and search for answers (which are not hard to find).

Exceptional but rings hollow in some aspects. There are no real upgrade trees and tracing is very docile. It isn't a replacement for Uplink, not in the slightest.  It's a streamlined system but there is something to be said about feeling like you're scavenging code and gaining abilities with every .exe you've dug out along the way. Who needs scrip when you have Script?

Hacknet should stand on its own as a Hack'Em Up-Lite. For what the campaign is, it is engaging and just about covers the surface of the culture of Data Specialists. Play for light-hearted script kiddie fun. Don't expect to learn how to actually pen-test. 

It's very much more improved with Workshop Content but the main campaign will be a great gateway for anyone just sinking their teeth into this sort of game. Recommend NT4, GreyHack and Uplink(OS) if they want anything a little deeper. NT4 will be the most bona fide, without requiring scripting on its own.

Playing this hacking game Hacknet. It really makes you feel like you're a hacker. This one mission I did, I had to hack another hacker. Once I got in there I realized I was in over my head because he had so many defenses up that I didn't have programs to hack with. The code:red buzzer starts to go off and before I knew it the countdown number was under 10 secs. I tried to cover my tracks by deleting my foot prints and then then tried to disconnect. But it was too late, this mother fucker already e-mailed me to tell me what a scrub I was lol. Then as the counter reached "0" he shut my PC down. As it rebooted I saw that he deleted most the boot programs on my computer. I literally had to rebuild my pc in DOS (not DOS but whatever the 'new' DOS is that people use) until I could reboot my system and start using it again. Wheew, I thought it was gone for good. I had to alt+tab during this process a couple times just to make sure it wasn't real. WOW! That was fun :D
